english.title: Master of a vessel fail to confirm delivery of a product that did not comply with import requirements

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: trade in animals and related products regulations 2011

english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being the master of a vessel, failed to confirm delivery of a product that did not comply with import requirements, namely **(..SPECIFY NATURE OF THE PRODUCT..), from a border inspection post by signing the certificate specified in Commission Decision 2000/571/EC, namely **(..SPECIFY THE CERTIFICATE..), and returning it as soon as was reasonably practicable to the official veterinary surgeon at the border inspection post from which it came
english.legislation: Contrary to paragraph 11 of Schedule 2 to and regulations 39 and 42(2) of the Trade in Animals and Related Products Regulations 2011.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
sent product did not comply with import requirements
from border inspection post to a ship
unaccompanied by certificate referred to in instrument in Sch 1

investigatoraction.description: Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum
Indictment: A fine

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
